title: What can you say about tongkat ali in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library gives no supported wording for tongkat ali, because no listed source supports one at a dose. Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats low testosterone (hypogonadism)".

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Natural Viagra, or works like erectile dysfunction drugs
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a drug or compares the product to one.
Promises to cure a medical condition.

evidence_gap: None of the four listed sources gives a use or a dose for tongkat ali. Health Canada's monograph list (checked 2026-10-14) has no tongkat ali or Eurycoma monograph, and none of the 14 Health Canada monographs read for this library mentions it. The ODS exercise and athletic performance fact sheet does not mention it; no other ODS fact sheet was checked. FDA's lists show no health claim for it. Regulation (EU) No 432/2012 lists no claim for it. Until a listed source covers it, the library supports no wording for it.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
